items.name: Tomatoes
items.description: Vine-ripened Lagos tomatoes, sold by the basket or the paint bucket. Firm enough for stew and sweet enough for salad.

items.name: Scotch Bonnet Pepper
items.description: The small, fiery pepper that gives Nigerian stew its heat. Sold fresh in mixed bowls or by the cup.

items.name: Okra
items.description: Tender green pods, best picked young. A staple for soup and the reason many stalls open before dawn.

items.name: Plantain
items.description: Sold in green, yellow and over-ripe bunches depending on whether you are frying, boiling or roasting.

items.name: Mango
items.description: Sweet, fibrous mangoes that arrive with the April rains and disappear by early October.

items.name: Pineapple
items.description: Golden, low-acid pineapple from the coastal belt, peeled to order at most stalls.

items.name: Sweet Corn
items.description: Boiled or roasted on the spot. The roadside favourites are picked the same morning in season.

items.name: Ugu (Fluted Pumpkin Leaves)
items.description: Fluted pumpkin leaves, shredded and sold by the bundle. The backbone of most Nigerian soups.

items.name: Waterleaf
items.description: Soft, quick-cooking greens used in edikang ikong and afang. Sold in tied bunches while still wet.

items.name: Brown Beans
items.description: Dried honey beans and oloyin, sold by the cup, the paint bucket or the bag.

items.name: Yam
items.description: Puna and white yam tubers, priced per tuber or per bundle. The new harvest lands with the dry season.

items.name: Watermelon
items.description: Heavy, deep-red melons that dominate the stalls through the hot months.
items.pick: Look for a heavy melon with a creamy-yellow field spot; that is where the sugar is.

items.name: Farm Eggs
items.description: Crates of free-range and deep-litter eggs from peri-urban poultry farms around Lagos.
